pages.text:
Crude Oil lies in deposits deep underground. The world is split into large regions, 8 chunks across, and each may hold one deposit: a round patch of chunks with its own kind, amount and depth. Deserts, oceans, badlands and plains have deposits more often, and bigger ones.
# Kinds
- Oil Seep: 1,000 to 3,000 buckets.
- Oil Pocket: 4,000 to 10,000.
- Oil Field: 12,000 to 30,000.
- Giant Oil Field: 40,000 to 100,000.
A deposit lies somewhere between Y -48 and Y 8.

# Oil caverns
In newly generated chunks every deposit is a real cavern full of oil: a sealed, flattened, roughly round chamber about twice as wide as it is tall, under the middle of its patch, one Crude Oil source block for every bucket it holds. A Giant Oil Field can be 70 blocks across.
A 2-block shell of stone or deepslate seals it, so caves, aquifers and lava never break in and the oil never leaks out. Crude Oil doesn't burn, so a cavern can't set a cave alight.
Some deposits are sour (see Sour Crude) and some have a gas cap: an empty dome at the top of the cavern, full of Natural Gas (see Natural Gas).

# One amount
The deposit's amount is what counts. Pumping takes from it, and so does anything that takes the oil's source blocks: a bucket, another mod's pump. Each source block is 1,000 mB. The oil in the cavern falls to match, a layer at a time from the top down, even in chunks that weren't loaded when it was pumped.
# Surface seeps
Above some Oil Seeps and Pockets in deserts and badlands, a small tar pit of Crude Oil marks the deposit below.
# Older chunks
A deposit reaching any chunk generated before caverns came in has no cavern: it stays invisible and works as it always has.

# Seismic Survey Tool
Use it on the ground: it tells you whether there's oil under this chunk, what kind of deposit it is, roughly how many buckets are left in it, how deep it lies, and in a cavern whether it's sour and has a gas cap. Walk the region to find its edges. With Paper in your inventory it also writes a Survey Record (see Survey Records).
# Getting it out
Build an Oil Derrick over the deposit: it drills down until it reaches the cavern, then leaves a Well Head. Build a Pumpjack round the Well Head to pump the oil out; it draws on the whole cavern. Several pumpjacks can share one deposit.
# Running dry
A Pumpjack slows as its deposit drains, down to a quarter of its full rate. A drained deposit never quite runs dry: every pumpjack on it still gets a trickle of 40 mB a second.
